STIF is a commercial and industrial company based in Saint-Georges-sur-Loire, a small town in the Maine-et-Loire area of western France, and it came up in a search for listed companies. Crunchbase gives no product description, so its exact products, customers and size cannot be confirmed from the data provided. Reported funding is about 41 million (currency as shown), most recently in June 2025. It is most likely a regional B2B business with little consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Alaska Power & Telephone (AP&T) is a utility holding company that owns small electric utilities, hydroelectric plants, local telephone companies and broadband networks serving remote communities in Southeast Alaska and parts of Washington state. Customers are residential and commercial households in isolated towns, paying regulated electricity and telecom rates plus internet subscriptions. It runs company-built hydro projects, a cable and fibre footprint and wholesale power sales. It has been largely employee-owned through an ESOP and trades over the counter under APTL. Founded 1957, it is regionally known, with no national consumer brand profile.

Betolar is a Finnish materials-technology company that develops Geoprime, a low-carbon binder that replaces cement in concrete by using industrial side streams such as slag, ash and mine tailings, plus an AI-supported Mix platform for designing mixes. Customers are concrete and precast producers, construction firms and industrial waste owners, paid through licences, material supply and project fees. Based in Kannonkoski, central Finland, it has been listed on Nasdaq First North Helsinki since 2021 and works with pilot partners in Europe and Asia. B2B climate-tech with low public awareness outside the construction sector.

Kalpataru Power Transmission is an Indian engineering, procurement and construction contractor that builds high-voltage power transmission lines and substations, oil and gas pipelines, railways, metro and urban infrastructure, and water systems. Customers are state utilities, power grid operators, oil and gas companies and governments across India, Africa, the Middle East, Europe and the Americas, including via subsidiaries JMC Projects and Linjemontage in Sweden. Part of the Kalpataru Group, it is listed on the NSE and BSE, now operating as Kalpataru Projects International. Order book runs to several billion dollars. B2B, with limited public brand recognition.

MDB Capital Group is a Texas-based venture and brokerage firm that focuses on early-stage deep-technology and patent-rich companies. Its model combines a public venture platform, Public Ventures, which sponsors IPOs of small technology companies, with investment banking, brokerage and advisory fees and returns from its own stakes. Founded by Christopher Marlett and Anthony DiGiandomenico, it is based in Addison, near Dallas, and listed on Nasdaq under MDBH after its 2023 IPO. It serves founders and retail and institutional investors, and has little consumer brand awareness, though it is known in small-cap finance circles.

Mintech is a South Korean company based in Daejeon, listed on the Korean market, with industries tagged as battery and business development. Crunchbase provides no product description and the funding figure shown, about 33.5 billion (currency as shown, likely Korean won), is from July 2023. From the tags, it appears to work in battery-related technology and materials, probably selling to industrial or electronics manufacturers rather than consumers. Its scale, customers and ownership cannot be confirmed from the data provided. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Mostalwar appears to be Mostostal Warszawa, a Polish construction and civil engineering contractor listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange under MSW. It builds roads, bridges, railways, industrial plants, stadiums, offices and logistics centres, working for Polish public bodies, infrastructure agencies and private developers. Majority-owned by the Spanish group Acciona since the 2000s, it is headquartered in Warsaw and has been active for roughly 70 years, with annual revenue historically in the range of a few hundred million euros to over a billion zloty. B2B and public-sector contractor with little consumer brand visibility.

Norsk Solar is a Norway-based renewable energy company in Stavanger that Crunchbase groups under energy and renewable energy, and it appeared in a search for listed companies. The data provided gives no product description, so its portfolio, such as solar parks owned or developed, cannot be confirmed here. Reported funding is about 29.8 million dollars, most recently January 2023. Likely a B2B or utility-facing solar developer or owner, with little consumer brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Prisma Properties is a Stockholm-based Swedish commercial real estate company that appeared in a search for listed companies. It is understood to own and manage commercial property such as logistics, light-industrial and office space, earning rental income from business tenants. Crunchbase lists no description, and the funding figure shown is SEK 250 million from January 2026, so details of portfolio size, tenants and exchange listing cannot be confirmed from the data provided. Property companies are B2B businesses with minimal consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Galapagos is a Belgian biotechnology company based in Mechelen, founded in 1999 and listed on Euronext Brussels and Nasdaq (GLPG). It discovered filgotinib, marketed as Jyseleca for rheumatoid arthritis and ulcerative colitis through its Gilead partnership, and built a CAR-T cell therapy business with decentralized manufacturing. Gilead paid $5 billion upfront in 2019 for rights and a stake. After setbacks it ended the Gilead collaboration on Jyseleca and in 2025 moved to wind down cell therapy. Revenue is collaboration-driven, employees number in the hundreds, and consumer awareness is low.

Horizon Pharma, later Horizon Therapeutics plc, was an Irish-domiciled biopharmaceutical company with major operations in Deerfield, Illinois, focused on rare, autoimmune and severe inflammatory diseases. Its main medicines were Tepezza for thyroid eye disease, Krystexxa for chronic gout and Uplizna, sold to specialist physicians and hospitals, mainly in the United States, and generating over 3 billion dollars of annual sales. It was listed on Nasdaq as HZNP. Amgen acquired the company for about 27.8 billion dollars in October 2023. Brand awareness is among prescribers, not consumers.

ANGUS Chemical is a specialty chemical producer, headquartered in Buffalo Grove, Illinois, making nitroalkanes and derivatives such as amino alcohols, oxazolidines and biocides used in paints and coatings, metalworking fluids, personal care, pharmaceutical intermediates and water treatment. Customers are industrial manufacturers, who buy it through long supply contracts. It runs a production site in Sterlington, Louisiana, and has changed ownership several times, with Dow owning it for a long period before a later private-equity sale, so current ownership should be checked. B2B ingredient supplier with low consumer visibility.

BGI Group is a Shenzhen-based genomics company founded in 1999 and a major player in DNA sequencing. Through listed units MGI Tech and BGI Genomics, it sells sequencers and reagents, runs genetic testing services including the NIFTY prenatal test, large population-genomics projects and COVID-19 tests. Customers are hospitals, research institutes, governments and labs in over 100 countries. The US placed several BGI entities on trade restriction lists, which complicates western partnerships. B2B and medical brand, with limited consumer recognition outside China, though a large organisation with thousands of employees.

EQRx was a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotechnology company founded by Alexis Borisy that aimed to develop and sell cancer and immunology drugs at much lower prices than existing therapies. Its pipeline included aumolertinib for lung cancer, licensed from Hansoh Pharma, and other small molecules in partnership with Chinese developers. It listed on Nasdaq via a SPAC merger in December 2021, raising over 1.8 billion dollars. In 2023 it agreed to merge with Revolution Medicines and the deal closed in November 2023. Never had a commercial product, so brand awareness was limited to biotech and investor circles.

Invitae was a San Francisco genetic testing company that offered clinical genetic panels for hereditary cancer, rare disease and reproductive health, plus oncology and consumer-facing genetics through its Ciitizen patient-records business. Customers were doctors, hospitals and patients, billed through insurers and direct payment. It listed on the NYSE (NVTA) in 2015, expanded through acquisitions such as Genelex and ArcherDX, and reached over 500 million dollars in annual revenue. It filed for Chapter 11 in February 2024 and its main assets were acquired by Labcorp in 2024. Known in healthcare, with little general consumer brand awareness.

SAGE Therapeutics was a Cambridge, Massachusetts neuroscience biopharma that developed Zulresso for postpartum depression, the first approved treatment of its kind, and Zurzuvae, an oral pill co-commercialised with Biogen from 2023. Customers are psychiatrists and obstetric care providers, with revenue from product sales and collaboration payments. Founded in 2010 and listed on Nasdaq (SAGE), it struggled after failed depression and Alzheimer's-related trials and cut staff. Supernus Pharmaceuticals agreed to acquire it in 2025 for roughly 795 million dollars. Brand awareness is among doctors, but Zurzuvae has a patient-facing marketing campaign.

Seagen, formerly Seattle Genetics, was a Bothell, Washington biotechnology company and a pioneer in antibody-drug conjugates for cancer. Its marketed products were Adcetris for lymphoma, Padcev for bladder cancer, Tivdak for cervical cancer and Tukysa for breast cancer, sold to oncologists worldwide with annual revenue of roughly 2 billion dollars. Founded in 1998 and listed on Nasdaq (SGEN), it was acquired by Pfizer for about 43 billion dollars, closing in December 2023, and now operates inside Pfizer Oncology. Brand awareness is among cancer specialists and investors.

Vingroup is Vietnam's largest private conglomerate, founded by billionaire Pham Nhat Vuong and headquartered in Hanoi. It spans real estate through Vinhomes and Vincom Retail, hospitality and resorts under Vinpearl, healthcare via Vinmec, education with Vinschool and VinUniversity, and electric vehicles through VinFast, which listed on Nasdaq in 2023 and sells cars in Vietnam, the US, Canada and Europe. Vingroup is listed on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (VIC) and employs tens of thousands. Very strong consumer brand across Vietnam and growing international visibility through VinFast, which has sponsored football events.

Gren is a Helsinki-based energy company, known as a producer of heat and power with district heating, electricity and gas operations tied to Nordic and Baltic cities. Crunchbase describes it simply as an energy utility services provider and the data provided gives no further detail. Funding of about 1.15 billion (currency as shown) is dated May 2026. Customers would be municipalities, households and industrial users, paying heating and energy fees, and the business would not carry a strong consumer brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Assertio is a US specialty pharmaceutical company, based in Lake Forest, Illinois, that acquires and sells branded medicines mainly for pain, neurology and inflammatory conditions. Products include Indocin suppositories and suspension, Otrexup (methotrexate auto-injector), Sympazan, Zipsor, Cambia and Rolvedon for neutropenia, sold to pharmacies and hospitals via wholesalers, with revenue of roughly 100 to 150 million dollars a year. Listed on Nasdaq (ASRT), it merged with Spectrum Pharmaceuticals in 2023 and has had heavy generic competition and debt restructuring. Brand awareness is among prescribers, not consumers.

BioInnovation Institute (BII) is a non-profit foundation-owned life science incubator in Copenhagen, funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation. It provides early-stage biotech, medtech and digital health startups with grants, lab space, coaching and a pre-seed programme, and runs a venture arm that backs early companies. It occupies a large campus in the Copenhagen Science City area and has hosted hundreds of ventures since launching in 2018. Customers are founders and investors, and income comes from foundation funding. Well known in the Nordic life science ecosystem, with little general consumer awareness.

IVERIC bio was a New Jersey ophthalmology biopharmaceutical company focused on retinal diseases. Its key product, Izervay (avacincaptad pegol), was approved by the FDA in 2023 as the second treatment for geographic atrophy, an advanced form of age-related macular degeneration, injected by retina specialists. Previously named Ophthotech, it listed on Nasdaq as ISEE. Astellas Pharma acquired it in 2023 for about 5.9 billion dollars, so it now operates as part of Astellas. Brand awareness is limited to eye doctors and healthcare investors, not consumers.

Taibang Biological Group is a Chinese plasma products company, tied to Shandong Taibang Biological Products, that collects human plasma at its own donation stations and produces human albumin, immunoglobulins and clotting factors. Customers are hospitals and distributors in China, supplied under heavy government regulation. It grew out of the former Nasdaq-listed China Biologic Products, which went private in 2020 and later restructured under Chinese ownership. Headquartered in Beijing, it is a large domestic plasma fractionator with thousands of employees. B2B healthcare brand, little consumer recognition, though known within Chinese hospital supply.

Trimble is a US technology company, based in Westminster, Colorado, that sells positioning, GPS, software and sensor systems. Its products serve construction (Tekla, SketchUp, machine control), geospatial surveying, agriculture and transportation fleets, sold to contractors, engineers, farmers and logistics firms through hardware plus subscription software. Founded in 1978 and listed on Nasdaq (TRMB), it employs around 12,000 people and earns about 3.5 billion dollars of annual revenue. In 2024 it moved its agriculture business into a joint venture with AGCO. B2B brand with strong industry recognition but low consumer awareness.

ViewRay was a medical device company based near Cleveland, Ohio, that made the MRIdian, an MRI-guided radiation therapy system that lets oncologists see tumours in real time while treating them. Customers were hospitals and cancer centres, with revenue from system sales, installation and service contracts across the US, Europe and Asia, and annual revenue of roughly 100 million dollars. It listed on Nasdaq (VRAY) in 2016 via a merger, struggled with cash burn and filed for bankruptcy in July 2023, with assets acquired by a successor. Brand known to radiation oncology staff, not consumers.

Apeel Sciences is a Goleta, California food technology company that makes Apeel, a plant-derived edible coating applied to fresh fruit and vegetables, such as avocados, citrus and cucumbers, to slow moisture loss and spoilage and extend shelf life. Customers are growers, packers, distributors and retailers including Costco, Kroger and Aldi, paying for coated produce or application services. Founded in 2012, it has raised over 700 million dollars from backers including Viking Global, Temasek, Bill Gates and Oprah Winfrey, and was valued around 2 billion dollars. B2B ingredient, visible to consumers only through a produce label.

AppHarvest was a Kentucky agritech company, based in Morehead, that built large high-tech greenhouses to grow tomatoes, cucumbers and leafy greens using recycled rainwater, selling to US grocers and food distributors under its own brand. Founded in 2018 by Jonathan Webb, it listed on Nasdaq (APPH) through a SPAC merger in February 2021 and attracted backing from celebrities and Martha Stewart. Chronic losses and operating problems led to a Chapter 11 filing in July 2023. Its consumer brand was limited to US grocery produce shelves and had modest awareness.

CymaBay Therapeutics was a California biopharmaceutical company, based in Newark, developing treatments for liver and rare metabolic diseases. Its lead drug, seladelpar, a PPAR-delta agonist for primary biliary cholangitis, showed strong late-stage results and was approved by the FDA in 2024 as Livdelzi. It was listed on Nasdaq (CBAY) and had no marketed product before the sale. Gilead Sciences acquired it for about 4.3 billion dollars, completed in March 2024. Brand awareness is among hepatologists and investors only, with no consumer profile.

Delta Hydrocarbons is a company in Utrecht, the Netherlands, tagged by Crunchbase under advanced materials and energy, whose description says it invests in field development and production. This suggests an upstream oil and gas investment vehicle, though the data provided does not name its assets, countries or owners. Reported funding is about 750 million dollars, but the date shown is March 2007, so figures are old and details should be verified. Energy investment firms of this kind are B2B with little consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

DST Global is an investment firm founded in 2009 by Russian-born entrepreneur Yuri Milner, active in late-stage technology investing and run from Hong Kong and London with offices elsewhere. It backed early Facebook, Twitter, Airbnb, Alibaba, Spotify, Uber, ByteDance, Stripe, Revolut, Flipkart and many Indian and Chinese internet leaders, using large growth rounds and concentrated stakes. Its income comes from returns on funds invested by institutional and private backers, with assets of tens of billions of dollars. A private investor with significant fame in tech finance but little consumer brand awareness.

DST Global, shown here as a second listing with the amount appended to the name, is the same investment firm founded in 2009 by Yuri Milner, based in London and Hong Kong. It invests in late-stage technology and internet companies, with past holdings including Facebook, Twitter, Airbnb, Alibaba, Spotify, ByteDance, Stripe and Flipkart. It raises capital from institutions and wealthy backers and earns returns on stakes, with assets in the tens of billions of dollars. A private fund with high standing among tech investors and no consumer brand profile. This row is a duplicate of the preceding DST Global entry.

IGM Biosciences was a Mountain View, California biotechnology company developing engineered IgM antibodies for cancer and autoimmune disease. Its lead candidate, imvotamab, targeted CD20 in lupus and other autoimmune conditions, and it worked with Sanofi on cancer programmes. Listed on Nasdaq as IGMS, it never had an approved product and burned substantial cash. In early 2025 it discontinued its clinical programmes, cut most staff and explored strategic options. Brand awareness was limited to biotech investors and specialist physicians, with no consumer recognition.

India Infrastructure Finance Company Limited (IIFCL) is a wholly government-owned Indian financial institution based in New Delhi, set up in 2006 to provide long-term loans for infrastructure such as roads, power, ports, airports and railways. It lends directly, refinances banks' infrastructure loans and takes part in bond and public-private partnership schemes, and it has a UK subsidiary for foreign currency financing. Clients are Indian developers and state agencies, and its balance sheet runs to many billions of dollars. A state-owned B2B lender with limited public brand recognition outside Indian finance circles.

MorphoSys was a German biotechnology company based in Planegg near Munich, known for antibody technology and for Monjuvi (tafasitamab) for lymphoma, marketed with Incyte, plus the myelofibrosis drug candidate pelabresib. It was listed on Nasdaq and Frankfurt (MOR) and earned money from royalties on partnered antibody discovery, such as Tremfya, and product sales. After acquiring Constellation Pharmaceuticals in 2021 it carried large losses. Novartis acquired MorphoSys for about 2.7 billion euros, completed in May 2024. Brand awareness is among oncologists and biotech investors, with no consumer profile.

Pliant Therapeutics is a South San Francisco clinical-stage biotechnology company developing treatments for fibrotic diseases. Its lead candidate, bexotegrast, a dual integrin inhibitor, was tested in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and primary sclerosing cholangitis, partnered earlier with Novartis. Listed on Nasdaq (PLRX), it has no marketed product and earns no product revenue. In 2025 its main trial was halted after safety concerns and the programme discontinued, leading to restructuring. Brand awareness is within biotech and investor circles, with none among consumers.

Shockwave Medical is a Santa Clara, California medical device company that makes intravascular lithotripsy systems, which use sonic pressure waves delivered through a catheter to break up calcified plaque in arteries, mainly in the heart and legs. Customers are hospitals and interventional cardiologists, with revenue from single-use catheters and generators, reaching roughly 730 million dollars in 2023. It listed on Nasdaq (SWAV) in 2019. Johnson & Johnson acquired it for about 13.1 billion dollars, closing in May 2024, and it now sits inside J&J MedTech. Brand awareness is among cardiologists, not consumers.

AC Milan is one of Europe's most successful football clubs, based in Milan, Italy, with seven European Cup and Champions League titles and 19 Serie A championships. It plays at the San Siro stadium, shared with Inter. Revenue, roughly 400 million euros a year, comes from broadcasting, commercial sponsorship and matchday sales. Sponsors include Emirates on the shirt and Puma as kit supplier. RedBird Capital Partners, led by Gerry Cardinale, bought the club from Elliott Management in 2022. Global fan base of hundreds of millions, and a long record of partnerships with major brands.

Ameropa is a privately owned Swiss agricultural trading group, headquartered in Binningen near Basel, founded in 1948. It trades and distributes fertilizers, grain and other agri commodities, and also owns fertilizer production and storage assets and agribusiness operations in Romania, Ukraine and other markets. Customers are farmers, cooperatives, processors and importers worldwide, and its revenue has run to many billions of dollars a year. The group is held by private owners and funded by banks. It is an agricultural supply chain business with low consumer brand awareness but strong standing among commodity traders.

Arcellx is a clinical-stage biotechnology company, founded in 2014 and based in Maryland with roots in Redwood City, California, developing CAR-T cell therapies for cancer. Its lead product, anitocabtagene autoleucel (anito-cel) for multiple myeloma, is being commercialised under a collaboration with Kite, a Gilead company, which shares costs and profits. Customers will be cancer hospitals and haematologists. Listed on Nasdaq (ACLX) since 2022, it earns collaboration income rather than product sales so far. Brand awareness is limited to oncology and investor communities, with no consumer profile.

Becton Dickinson India is the Indian subsidiary of BD (Becton, Dickinson and Company), the Franklin Lakes, New Jersey medical technology group listed on the NYSE (BDX). BD makes syringes, needles, IV catheters, diagnostic instruments, specimen collection and infusion pumps, sold to hospitals, labs and health systems, with annual revenue around 20 billion dollars and roughly 70,000 employees. The Indian unit sells and manufactures disposable devices locally. In 2025 BD agreed to merge its biosciences and diagnostics business with Waters. Strong in healthcare supply, but little consumer awareness.

Nimbus Therapeutics is a Boston-based biotechnology company founded in 2009 that uses computational physics-based modelling to design small-molecule drugs against hard targets. Its TYK2 inhibitor programme was sold to Takeda in 2022 in a deal worth up to 6 billion dollars including 4 billion dollars upfront, and it continues to pursue cancer and metabolic programmes such as ACC and WRN inhibitors. It is venture-backed and privately held, with investors including Atlas Venture and Bill Gates-linked funds. B2B science brand with recognition only among pharma and investors.

Novaland Group is a major Vietnamese real estate developer headquartered in Ho Chi Minh City, listed on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (NVL). It builds large mixed-use townships and resort projects such as Aqua City, NovaWorld Phan Thiet and NovaWorld Ho Tram, selling apartments, villas and condotels to Vietnamese consumers and investors and partnering with international brands in hospitality. Founded in 1992, it was hit by a property and bond-market crunch from 2022, with debt restructuring. Strong regional brand in Vietnam's property market and visible through consumer-facing marketing.

Octal is an Omani manufacturer of PET sheet used in thermoformed packaging such as food trays, clamshells and bottles, and it makes recycled PET sheet too. It describes itself as a global supplier of clear rigid packaging materials, with plants in Salalah, Oman and later sites in Europe and elsewhere, serving packaging converters and food and consumer goods firms in over 80 countries. Its output is among the world's largest in the segment. Based in Muscat, it is a private industrial group. B2B materials brand with little consumer visibility.

RefleXion Medical is a Hayward, California medical technology company that makes the X1, a radiotherapy system combining a linear accelerator with PET imaging, called biology-guided radiotherapy, which lets the machine track tumours using their own emitted signals and treat multiple lesions. Customers are hospitals and cancer centres that buy systems and service contracts. Founded in 2009 by Sam Mazin, it is venture-backed and privately held, with the X1 cleared by the FDA. Brand awareness is among radiation oncologists, not consumers.

Syros Pharmaceuticals was a Watertown, Massachusetts biotechnology company that studied gene control to develop cancer medicines. Its lead candidate, tamibarotene, was being developed for myelodysplastic syndrome and acute myeloid leukaemia, along with SY-2101 for acute promyelocytic leukaemia. Listed on Nasdaq (SYRS) after its 2016 IPO, it never had an approved product. After the pivotal MDS trial failed in 2024 it cut most staff, and it later explored strategic alternatives and wound down. Known only in oncology and investor circles, with no consumer profile.

Thirteen Group is a not-for-profit housing association headquartered in Middlesbrough, North East England. It owns and manages roughly 34,000 social and affordable rented homes across Teesside, County Durham and North Yorkshire, builds new homes, and offers repairs, community and support services to its tenants. Revenue comes from rents, shared ownership and development sales, with annual turnover in the low hundreds of millions of pounds. A well-known social landlord in the region, but a community brand, with limited national consumer visibility.

Adaptimmune is a UK-founded cell therapy company based in Abingdon, Oxfordshire, with a large US base in Pennsylvania, developing engineered T cell receptor therapies for solid tumours. Its Tecelra (afami-cel) was approved by the FDA in August 2024 for synovial sarcoma, the first engineered T cell receptor therapy for a solid tumour, and it has other candidates such as lete-cel. Listed on Nasdaq (ADAP), it had collaborations with GSK and Astellas. In 2025, facing cash needs, it sold its commercial assets to US WorldMeds. Brand awareness is among oncologists, with no consumer profile.

Berlin Packaging is a Chicago-based supplier of glass, plastic and metal containers, closures and dispensing systems, positioned as a hybrid packaging supplier and consultant. It sells bottles, jars and tubes plus design, financing and supply-chain services to thousands of food, beverage, cosmetic, pharmaceutical and household brands, with many sold directly to small and mid-sized customers. Founded in 1969, it has over 100 locations worldwide and annual sales above 3 billion dollars. Private-equity backed, with Oak Hill Capital and Investcorp among investors. B2B packaging brand with limited consumer awareness.

BioNexus Gene Lab is a Kuala Lumpur-based Malaysian company listed on Nasdaq (BGLC), operating in genomic testing and chemicals. Its Chemrex subsidiary distributes industrial chemicals across Southeast Asia and generates most of its revenue, while the genomics unit offers health screening, including blood-based tests aimed at cancer risk and preventive care. Customers are industrial buyers, clinics and individual patients. Small-cap, with revenue in the millions of dollars, and little brand awareness beyond Malaysia.

Encoded Therapeutics is a South San Francisco biotechnology company, founded in 2015, developing gene therapies that use regulatory DNA elements delivered with AAV vectors to switch genes on in the right cells, aimed mainly at severe genetic neurological disorders such as Dravet syndrome and other epilepsies. Its lead programme, ETX101, is in clinical testing. Customers would be neurologists and hospitals once approved. Privately held and venture-backed, with investors including Sofinnova and Fidelity and over 500 million dollars raised in total. Brand awareness is limited to biotech circles.

Evofem Biosciences is a San Diego women's health company whose only commercial product is Phexxi, a hormone-free vaginal gel contraceptive that regulates vaginal pH. It sells to women in the US through pharmacies, telehealth partners and direct-to-consumer advertising, and also promotes Soaanz, a heart-failure drug it acquired the rights to. It became public through a 2018 merger with Neothetics and was listed on Nasdaq (EVFM) before moving to over-the-counter trading. Revenue is in the tens of millions of dollars, with heavy debt. Consumer-facing brand with national advertising but modest awareness.

Ezdan Holding Group is Qatar's largest real estate company, headquartered in Doha and listed on the Qatar Stock Exchange (ERES). It owns and manages residential towers, compounds, villas, retail malls such as Ezdan Mall, hotels and serviced apartments, and also develops land and offers property services. Customers are expatriate and Qatari households, companies and tourists, paying rents, hotel fees and sales. The group is chaired by Sheikh Thani bin Abdullah bin Thani Al Thani and holds a substantial share of the country's rental housing. The Crunchbase description about cybersecurity looks wrong. Recognised across Qatar as a consumer-facing property brand.

Formation Bio is a New York-based pharmaceutical company, formerly Tech and Bio and earlier Triplet Therapeutics, that uses AI and data tools to speed drug development. Rather than doing early discovery, it buys or licenses assets from other developers and runs clinical development with its AI platform, working with Sanofi and OpenAI on tools. Founded in 2016 by Benjamin Liu, Tom Beadle and Chris Bohn, it raised a 372 million dollar Series D in 2024 from Andreessen Horowitz, Thrive and Sanofi, bringing total funding to over 500 million dollars. Privately held, known mainly in biotech and venture circles.

K+S is a German mining and salt company based in Kassel, listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange (SDF) and part of the MDAX. It produces potash and magnesium fertilizers sold to farmers, industrial salts for chemical and food uses, de-icing salt, and consumer products such as pet litter and table salt under brands like Esco. Operations include mines in Germany and the Bethune potash mine in Saskatchewan, Canada, with annual revenue of roughly 3 to 4 billion euros and about 11,000 employees. Founded in 1889 as Kali und Salz. Mostly B2B, with some consumer salt products, and recognised in Germany.

Metsera was a New York clinical-stage biotechnology company developing injectable and oral treatments for obesity and related conditions, built around monthly GLP-1 and amylin candidates such as MET-097i and MET-233i. Founded by ARCH Venture Partners and Population Health Partners, it listed on Nasdaq (MTSR) in January 2025 and had no approved drug. In November 2025 Pfizer acquired the company for up to about 10 billion dollars after a bidding contest with Novo Nordisk. Brand awareness is among investors and pharma, with none among consumers.

Moatable is a US-based software holding company, formerly the Chinese social network Renren, which listed on the NYSE in 2011 and was later renamed. Its main business is Chime, a cloud CRM and marketing platform for real estate agents and brokerages, and it also owns Trucker Path, a mobile app and trucking-services platform used by long-haul truck drivers in North America. Revenue comes from software subscriptions and services. Listed on Nasdaq (MTBL) and operating from Phoenix, Arizona, it is a small-cap SaaS business with strong niche recognition among agents and truckers but little general awareness.

NGM Biopharmaceuticals was a South San Francisco biotechnology company researching therapies for liver, metabolic and retinal diseases, founded in 2007 with backing from Merck, which held a major collaboration and stake. Its pipeline included aldafermin for fatty liver disease, which failed in trials, and later antibody candidates for age-related eye disease and obesity. It was listed on Nasdaq (NGM) from 2019 and earned revenue from Merck collaboration payments. In 2024 it agreed to a take-private deal led by The Column Group and other investors, ending its public listing. Brand awareness only in biotech circles.

Opthea is an Australian biotechnology company, based in Melbourne and listed on the ASX (OPT) with Nasdaq ADSs, developing sozinibercept, an injection used with standard anti-VEGF drugs for wet age-related macular degeneration. It ran two large Phase 3 trials, ShORe and COAST, and had financing and partnership arrangements with Carlyle and others. In early 2025 the trials failed to meet their main goals, which cut its value sharply and led to restructuring. Customers would have been retina specialists, and the company had no marketed product. Brand awareness is limited to ophthalmology and investor communities.

PL Developments is a Westbury, New York manufacturer of private-label over-the-counter health products, including liquid and softgel medicines, vitamins and supplements, as well as personal care items, sold under retailers' own store brands, primarily to US drugstore, grocery and mass-market chains. It operates several US factories and distribution sites, with Time-Cap Labs a notable subsidiary, and employs thousands of people. Reported funding of about 500 million dollars is from October 2024 and is probably debt financing. B2B with essentially no consumer brand of its own. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Regulus Therapeutics was a San Diego clinical-stage biotechnology company developing microRNA-targeted medicines. Its lead candidate, farabursen (RGLS8429), was in development for autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease, a genetic kidney condition, with Phase 3 plans after strong mid-stage data. It listed on Nasdaq (RGLS) and held a deal with Sanofi earlier in its life. Novartis agreed to acquire Regulus in April 2025 for up to 1.7 billion dollars, including milestone payments, and the deal closed that year. No marketed product and brand awareness limited to biotech and kidney disease specialists.

Savannah Cement is a Kenyan cement producer based in Nairobi, with its manufacturing site at Athi River near the capital, supplying construction and building-materials customers in Kenya and the region. Crunchbase describes it as a building materials specialist and lists reported funding of about 500 million dollars, with the most recent entry in April 2023, though the exact transaction is not explained in the data provided. Ownership, capacity and revenue cannot be confirmed here. Cement is a B2B product bought by contractors and dealers with little consumer brand awareness outside East Africa. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

VBI Vaccines, formerly SciVac, was a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company developing vaccines and virus-like particle technology, headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts, with research and manufacturing in Ottawa, Canada, and operations in Israel. Its main product, PreHevbrio, was a three-antigen hepatitis B vaccine for adults that was approved in the US in 2021. It also had COVID-19 and glioblastoma candidates. Listed on Nasdaq (VBIV), it ran into funding problems and in 2024 filed for creditor protection and sold off its assets. Customers were physicians and public health agencies. Brand awareness limited to healthcare and investors.

Ventyx Biosciences is a San Diego clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing oral NLRP3 inflammasome inhibitors and other small molecules for inflammatory disease, targeting conditions such as obesity-related inflammation, Parkinson's disease and cardiovascular disease. Founded in 2018 and listed on Nasdaq (VTYX), it has no approved product and relies on investor capital. Eli Lilly agreed in early 2026 to acquire the company for about 1.2 billion dollars. Customers would be specialist physicians once drugs are approved. Brand awareness is limited to pharma and investors, with no consumer profile.

Abeona Therapeutics is a Cleveland, Ohio gene and cell therapy company whose lead product, Zevaskyn (prademagene zamikeracel), received FDA approval in April 2025 for recessive dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa, a rare blistering skin disease. It uses patients' own gene-corrected skin cells grafted as sheets, and customers are specialised treatment centres paid through insurers at a price in the hundreds of thousands of dollars. Listed on Nasdaq (ABEO), it earlier explored AAV gene therapy programmes for eye and metabolic diseases. Brand awareness is among rare disease clinicians, patients and investors.

Akebia Therapeutics is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biopharmaceutical company focused on kidney disease. Its products are Vafseo (vadadustat), an oral drug for anaemia due to chronic kidney disease in dialysis patients, approved in the US in 2024, and Auryxia (ferric citrate) for phosphate control and iron deficiency. Customers are nephrologists and dialysis providers including large chains, with revenue from product sales of over 150 million dollars. Listed on Nasdaq (AKBA) and founded in 2007. Brand awareness is mostly among kidney specialists and investors, not consumers.

Anticimex is a Stockholm-based pest control company founded in 1934, one of the largest in the world. It sells pest extermination, prevention and hygiene services, and is known for its SMART digital pest control, which uses connected traps that detect rodents and send alerts. Customers are businesses such as restaurants, food factories and property owners, plus households, with operations in over 20 countries in Europe, North America, Asia and Australia and around 10,000 staff. It is privately held with private-equity backing and has made many bolt-on acquisitions. B2B and local service brand with moderate recognition in the Nordics.

Apollo Therapeutics is a Cambridge, UK clinical-stage biotechnology company that develops drugs licensed from universities and large pharma partners, built as a shared-risk model with several big pharma backers, among them AstraZeneca, GSK and Johnson & Johnson. Its portfolio covers immunology, inflammation and metabolic diseases and includes antibody and small-molecule candidates in early and mid-stage trials. It has raised nearly 400 million dollars, including a large round in 2023, and is privately held. Customers would be physicians once products are approved. A B2B science company with recognition only in UK and global biotech circles.

Applied Therapeutics is a New York biopharmaceutical company developing treatments for rare metabolic diseases. Its lead candidate, govorestat (AT-007), an aldose reductase inhibitor, targets classic galactosemia and sorbitol dehydrogenase deficiency, and it also studied it for diabetic cardiomyopathy. The FDA declined to approve it for galactosemia in November 2024, leaving it with no marketed product and a restructuring. Founded in 2016 and listed on Nasdaq (APLT), it serves rare-disease specialists and families. Brand awareness is limited to patient communities and investors.

Areteia Therapeutics is a New Jersey-based biopharmaceutical company launched in 2023 with a large Series A, built around dexpramipexole, an oral drug for eosinophilic asthma, licensed from Knopp Biosciences. It has run Phase 3 trials in patients with uncontrolled asthma and plans other eosinophil-related diseases. Customers would be respiratory specialists and patients if approved. Privately held and venture-backed, with funding of about 425 million dollars. A B2B biotech with no meaningful consumer brand awareness.

BillionToOne is a Menlo Park, California molecular diagnostics company founded in 2016, known for Unity, a prenatal blood test that screens for genetic conditions in the fetus using small amounts of DNA, and Northstar, a liquid-biopsy test used to monitor cancer treatment. Customers are obstetricians, oncologists and health systems, paid mainly through insurers and direct billing, with revenue in the hundreds of millions of dollars and strong growth. It listed on Nasdaq (BLLN) in 2025. Brand awareness is among clinicians, with some patient-facing marketing for prenatal screening.

Biodesix is a Colorado diagnostics company based in Louisville that makes blood-based tests for lung disease. Its main product is Nodify, a test pair that helps doctors decide whether lung nodules found on scans are likely cancer, along with the GeneStrat and Nodify Lung testing family, and it earns revenue from testing and from biopharma services work. Customers are physicians and health systems, billed through insurers and Medicare. Listed on Nasdaq (BDSX), with annual revenue of roughly 60 to 70 million dollars. Brand awareness is among pulmonologists.

Cellectis is a Paris-based biotechnology company, founded in 1999, that uses TALEN gene editing to create allogeneic CAR-T cell therapies off-the-shelf from healthy donor cells for blood cancers. It listed on Euronext Paris and Nasdaq (CLLS), and AstraZeneca is its largest shareholder after a 2023 investment. Other partners include Servier and Allogene, which licenses its UCART candidates, and it also has a plant gene editing unit. Customers would be haematology and oncology centres. Brand awareness is among cell therapy and biotech investors, not consumers.

Charlotte's Web is a Colorado-based hemp-derived CBD wellness company, founded by the Stanley brothers, whose products include gummies, oils, capsules, topicals and pet products, sold online and through more than 10,000 retail stores in the US. The brand grew out of a hemp strain used for a child's epilepsy, and it is one of the best known CBD consumer brands, though sales shrank after the market boom faded. Listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange (CWEB) with US over-the-counter shares, it produces on its own farms in Colorado. Strong US consumer awareness in the CBD category.

Compart Systems is a Malaysia-based manufacturer in Kulim, Kedah, of high-purity components and sub-systems for semiconductor and industrial gas delivery, such as valves, regulators and fittings, with operations in Asia and the US. Crunchbase describes it as a global strategic supplier but the text is cut off, so detail on customers, ownership and size cannot be confirmed from the data provided. Funding of 398 million dollars dates from December 2020, which may be a buyout or recapitalisation. It is a B2B component supplier with no consumer brand. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

CPM Holdings is a Blaine, Minnesota industrial engineering group that supplies machinery and consumables for animal feed, pet food, biomass and oilseed processing. Its brands include California Pellet Mill, CPM Roskamp Champion, Beta Raven and Extru-Tech, selling pellet mills, extruders, flaking mills and process automation to feed manufacturers, grain processors and food companies in more than 100 countries. With roots going back to the 1800s, it has several thousand employees and annual revenue approaching 1 billion dollars. Privately held and long owned by private equity. B2B equipment maker, known in agriculture but not to consumers.

F2G is a Manchester, UK biotechnology company developing antifungal drugs for life-threatening invasive infections, notably olorofim, a first-in-class drug against moulds such as Aspergillus that resist standard treatment. The FDA declined to approve olorofim in 2023, requesting more data, and the company continues the programme through a confirmatory trial. Founded in 2008 as a spin-out, it is private and venture-funded, with the most recent round in September 2024. Brand awareness is among infectious disease specialists.

Guardian Pharmacy Services is an Atlanta, Georgia provider of medication management and pharmacy services for long-term care. It supplies prescriptions packaged by dose to assisted living, behavioural health and group homes, working through a network of roughly 50 pharmacies in over 40 states, and it generates about 1.2 billion dollars in annual revenue. Founded in 1983 and led by the Pittman and Dickinson families, it listed on the NYSE (GRDN) in September 2024. Customers are care facilities and residents. A B2B healthcare service brand with little consumer recognition. The Georgia country label refers to the US state.

Joincare Pharmaceutical Group is a Shenzhen-based Chinese pharmaceutical company, listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, that makes branded and generic medicines, active pharmaceutical ingredients and diagnostics. Its main areas are respiratory drugs including inhaled products, gastrointestinal products, and anti-infective drugs, and it controls the listed company Livzon Pharmaceutical. Customers are hospitals, pharmacies and distributors across China, with some exports of ingredients. Annual revenue runs to several billion dollars. Mostly a B2B pharma brand, with a degree of consumer recognition in China through OTC products.

Kernel Holding is a Ukrainian agribusiness group headquartered in Kyiv, listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (KER) and run by Andriy Verevskyi. It is the largest sunflower oil producer and a major exporter of Ukrainian grain, oilseeds and bottled oil, farming several hundred thousand hectares and operating oilseed crushing plants, grain silos and a Black Sea port terminal. Customers are food processors, traders and retailers across Europe, Asia and the Middle East. The war in Ukraine has disrupted operations and export routes. Mainly B2B, with bottled oil sold under consumer brands in Ukraine.

Mainstay Medical is a medical device company, founded in Ireland and listed on Euronext Paris before delisting, whose ReActiv8 implantable neurostimulation system treats chronic low back pain by stimulating nerves to the multifidus muscle to help restore control of the lower back. Customers are pain specialists and spine surgeons, with US commercial operations run from San Diego. The system holds FDA approval and CE marking. Revenue has been in the low tens of millions of dollars, with total funding of about 395 million dollars. Brand awareness is among doctors and patients with chronic back pain.

Mereo BioPharma is a London and Redwood City biotechnology company, listed on Nasdaq (MREO), developing rare disease and oncology drugs. Its lead candidate setrusumab, an antibody against sclerostin, is being developed by partner Ultragenyx for osteogenesis imperfecta (brittle bone disease), with milestones and royalties owed to Mereo. It also has alvelestat for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency lung disease. The company has no marketed product, a small team and revenue from partnerships. Setrusumab's pivotal trial results in 2025 were disappointing for investors. Brand awareness is among rare disease clinicians and investors.

Molecular Templates was an Austin, Texas clinical-stage biotechnology company developing engineered toxin bodies, protein-based drugs that deliver a bacterial-derived toxin to kill cancer cells. Its candidates included MT-6402 and MT-5111 for HER2-positive cancers, and it had a partnership with Bristol Myers Squibb through Celgene, as well as with Takeda. Listed on Nasdaq (MTEM), it had no marketed product and struggled with funding, laying off staff in 2023 and 2024 and winding down operations soon after. Brand awareness was confined to biotech investors and oncology researchers.

OCI Partners LP was a Texas master limited partnership, based in Nederland near Beaumont, that owned a methanol and ammonia production complex. It sold methanol and ammonia to industrial customers such as chemical and fertilizer companies under contracts and spot sales, and it was a subsidiary of Dutch fertilizer group OCI N.V. Listed on the NYSE (OCIP) from its 2013 IPO, it had a plant capacity of about 912,000 tons of methanol and 365,000 tons of ammonia a year. OCI bought out the public units in 2018. B2B commodity chemical supplier with no consumer brand awareness.

Quanta Dialysis Technologies is a Warwick, UK medical technology company that makes the SC+ haemodialysis system, a compact machine designed for use at home or in clinics, with a cartridge-based, easy-to-operate set-up. Founded in 2008, it has CE marking, UK approval and FDA clearance, and sells to dialysis providers, hospitals and national health services. Total funding is about 410 million dollars, with several private healthcare investors. It is private, with a small-to-mid-sized workforce. Brand awareness is among kidney specialists and renal care companies, not the public.

Scorpion Therapeutics was a Boston biotechnology company developing precision oncology medicines, notably STX-478, a mutant-selective PI3K-alpha inhibitor for breast and other cancers that spares healthy cells. Founded in 2020 by Keith Flaherty and others, it was backed by Third Rock Ventures and raised hundreds of millions of dollars from investors. Eli Lilly agreed to acquire it in January 2025 for up to 2.5 billion dollars, with the deal completed that year, and the programme continues inside Lilly. It had no marketed product and brand awareness was limited to biotech and oncology circles.

scPharmaceuticals is a Burlington, Massachusetts pharmaceutical company that developed and sells Furoscix, a subcutaneous infusion of furosemide delivered through an on-body device, to treat fluid congestion in heart failure and chronic kidney disease patients at home, avoiding hospital admission. Customers are cardiologists, hospitals and patients, billed through insurance. Listed on Nasdaq (SCPH), it reached roughly 60 million dollars in annual sales in 2024. MannKind agreed to acquire it in 2025 for about 360 million dollars. Brand awareness is among cardiologists and heart failure clinics.

Torrent Pharmaceuticals is an Indian drugmaker based in Ahmedabad and part of the Torrent Group, listed on the NSE and BSE. It specialises in chronic therapies, particularly cardiovascular, central nervous system, gastroenterology and diabetes medicines, and sells branded generics in India, Brazil, Germany, the US and other markets, with annual revenue of around 1 billion dollars or more. It acquired Curatio Healthcare in 2022 and moved to take majority control of JB Chemicals in 2025. Well known to Indian doctors and pharmacies, with strong visibility among OTC and prescription brands, though little recognition abroad.

TScan Therapeutics is a Waltham, Massachusetts clinical-stage biotechnology company developing T cell receptor engineered T cell therapies. Its lead programmes, TSC-101 and TSC-100, are aimed at preventing relapse in blood cancers such as acute myeloid leukaemia after stem cell transplant, and it also has solid-tumour candidates and a discovery platform to find T cell targets. Listed on Nasdaq (TCRX) since 2021, it is funded by investors and a partnership with Amgen and Novartis, and has no product revenue. Brand awareness is among cancer specialists and biotech investors.

ADARx Pharmaceuticals is a San Diego genetic medicine company developing RNA-based drugs, mainly small interfering RNA (siRNA) and RNA-editing therapies, delivered with its own chemistry and conjugation platform. Its programmes target cardiovascular, metabolic and neurological diseases, and it has collaborations with pharma partners. Founded in 2020 and venture-backed, it raised a large Series C in 2025, bringing total funding to about 332 million dollars. Privately held and pre-revenue, so customers would be physicians if medicines are approved. Brand awareness limited to RNA therapeutics and investor circles.

AgDevCo is a London-based specialist investor in agriculture and agribusiness in Sub-Saharan Africa, providing patient capital to farms, processors and food supply chains, such as horticulture, dairy, grains, aquaculture and cold storage. Founded in 2009 with funding from the UK government and other development backers, including the Gates Foundation, it makes equity and debt investments and works with local entrepreneurs, aiming for both financial return and jobs and food security. It holds investments in countries including Zambia, Ghana, Nigeria and Tanzania. B2B development finance firm, little consumer visibility.

Alebund Pharmaceuticals is a Shanghai biopharmaceutical company, active in kidney and metabolic disease, developing treatments for chronic kidney disease complications. Its lead candidate AP301 is a phosphate binder, a drug for lowering high phosphate in dialysis patients and it is running late-stage studies in China with US plans. Founded in 2015 and backed by venture and healthcare funds, it raised hundreds of millions of dollars in total, including a Series C in January 2025. Brand awareness is among nephrologists.

Andela is a New York-headquartered talent marketplace that connects companies with vetted remote software engineers, data specialists and AI professionals, many based in Africa and other emerging markets. It started in 2014 as a training programme for African developers, founded by Jeremy Johnson and others, with backing from Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, Google and Softbank, and raised 200 million dollars in 2021 at a 1.5 billion dollar valuation. Customers are tech and enterprise firms who pay per engineer placement or contract. Private, with thousands of engineers on its network. B2B, well known in tech hiring, little consumer awareness.

Avalyn Pharma is a Boston-area and Seattle-based clinical-stage company developing inhaled versions of existing lung drugs, notably inhaled pirfenidone (AP01) and inhaled nintedanib (AP02) for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and other progressive pulmonary fibrosis, which aim to reduce the stomach and liver side effects of the oral forms. Customers would be pulmonologists and patients if approved. Privately held and backed by venture investors, with funding of about 372 million dollars including a round in July 2025. It has no marketed product, and brand awareness is limited to respiratory specialists and biotech investors.

Be Biopharma is a Cambridge, Massachusetts biotechnology company, born from Harvard-linked science and Atlas Venture, that engineers a patient's B cells to produce therapeutic proteins in the body, an approach it calls B cell medicines. Targets include rare genetic conditions such as haemophilia and enzyme deficiencies, with the aim of a one-time treatment that can be re-dosed. It raised a 130 million dollar Series B in 2023 from Atlas Venture and other investors, and later rounds, bringing total funding to about 356 million dollars. Private and pre-revenue, known in biotech circles.

BioAtla is a San Diego clinical-stage biotechnology company that develops conditionally active biologic antibodies, designed to be active only inside the tumour microenvironment to limit side effects. Its programmes include mecbotamab vedotin (BA3011) and ozuriftamab vedotin (BA3021), antibody-drug conjugates for sarcoma and head and neck cancer, plus cell therapy collaborations. Listed on Nasdaq (BCAB), it has no marketed product and relies on investor funding, with funding totalling about 340 million dollars. Brand awareness is among oncologists and biotech investors, with no consumer profile.

Bionano Genomics is a San Diego life sciences instrumentation and diagnostics company. Its Saphyr system performs optical genome mapping, imaging very long DNA molecules to detect large structural variants that standard sequencing misses, used in research and genetic disease testing. It also owns the Lineagen and BioDiscovery businesses and runs clinical testing services. Customers are laboratories, hospitals and research institutes, with annual revenue of around 30 million dollars. Listed on Nasdaq (BNGO), it has had heavy losses, a reverse split and restructuring. Brand awareness is among genomics scientists.

Capricor Therapeutics is a San Diego clinical-stage biotechnology company developing cell and exosome therapies. Its lead candidate, deramiocel (CAP-1002), is a cardiac-derived cell therapy for Duchenne muscular dystrophy cardiomyopathy, and the company also works on exosome vaccine platforms. The FDA issued a complete response letter in 2025, delaying approval, and the company is pursuing further data. Listed on Nasdaq (CAPR), it has a distribution agreement with Nippon Shinyaku and no product revenue. Customers would be neuromuscular specialists and Duchenne families. Brand awareness is strong within the Duchenne community, with little elsewhere.

Chime Biologics is a Wuhan, China-based contract development and manufacturing organisation (CDMO) for biologic drugs, with funding of about 332 million dollars in recent rounds. As described in Crunchbase it is a biopharmaceutical company, which indicates it provides process development and commercial manufacturing of antibodies and other biologics for domestic and international drug developers. It is likely a B2B service provider with little consumer awareness. Details of its ownership, capacity and customers cannot be confirmed from the data provided. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

CloudBees is a San Jose, California software company that sells enterprise software delivery tools built on Jenkins, the open-source automation server, including CloudBees CI, CD, feature management and security products. Founded in 2010 by Sacha Labourey, it serves large organisations such as banks, telecom and technology companies that need to build, test and release software at scale, charging subscription fees. It has raised over 350 million dollars, with Goldman Sachs, Lightspeed and Matrix among investors, reached a valuation above 1 billion dollars, and has a few hundred employees. B2B developer brand with little consumer awareness.

Corbus Pharmaceuticals is a Norwood, Massachusetts clinical-stage oncology and obesity biopharmaceutical company, listed on Nasdaq (CRBP). Its lead programme is CRB-701, an antibody-drug conjugate targeting Nectin-4 for cancers like head and neck, bladder and cervical cancer, licensed from the Chinese company CSPC, and it also has CB1-targeted drug candidates for obesity. It earlier developed lenabasum for autoimmune diseases, which failed in trials, leading it to change focus. No marketed product and no consumer profile, with brand awareness limited to oncology and biotech investors.

D3 Bio is a Chinese biotechnology company with a base in Wuxi, Jiangsu, and an office in Shanghai, focused on developing targeted cancer medicines. Its best-known programme is D3S-001, a next-generation inhibitor of the KRAS G12C mutation, studied in lung and colorectal cancers, and it is understood to have raised funds from venture and strategic backers, with total reported funding of 370 million dollars in December 2025. It is privately held and pre-commercial, so customers would be oncologists and hospitals in future. B2B science brand with little consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Dewpoint Therapeutics is a Boston biotechnology company, founded in 2018 from research by Whitehead Institute scientists Richard Young and Anthony Hyman, that targets biomolecular condensates, droplet-like structures inside cells that organise biological activity. It screens for small molecules that change condensate behaviour and aims to treat cancer, neurodegeneration and other disease areas. It has pharma collaborations with Bayer and Merck and raised over 360 million dollars from institutional investors, and cut staff after strategy changes. Private and pre-revenue. Known in biotech circles, with none among consumers.

Dizal Pharma is a Shanghai-based biopharmaceutical company founded in 2017, focused on oral targeted therapies for cancer and immune diseases. Its main products are sunvozertinib (Zegfrovy), a drug for EGFR exon 20 insertion lung cancer approved in China in 2023 and later by the FDA on an accelerated basis, and golidocitinib for lymphoma. Customers are oncologists and hospitals, with sales in China and growing global partnerships. It has pursued a listing on Shanghai's STAR Market. Funding is about 346 million dollars. Brand awareness is among cancer doctors and Asian biotech investors, with little consumer visibility.

ECI Group appears in the data as a real estate and construction property-management business located in Atlanta, Georgia. Crunchbase describes it as operating in real estate and providing services across several segments, but the text is cut off and the data provided does not say who it serves, what it builds or how large it is. Reported funding is about 350 million dollars, most recently in October 2024, which may be a financing round or debt facility. Real estate groups are usually B2B with limited public brand awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Exagen is a Vista, California diagnostics company that develops and sells tests for autoimmune rheumatic diseases, mainly lupus and rheumatoid arthritis. Its flagship AVISE test portfolio includes AVISE CTD, a connective-tissue-disease panel built around cell-bound complement activation products, and AVISE SLE+ and AVISE Lupus tests, and it also offers drug-monitoring tests for hydroxychloroquine. Customers are rheumatologists, billed through insurers and Medicare, with annual revenue of roughly 50 to 60 million dollars. Listed on Nasdaq (XGN) since 2019. Brand awareness is among rheumatologists and patients with autoimmune disease.

Giganet is a UK communications business based in Fareham, Hampshire, which Crunchbase describes as a communications platform offering services to business, covering customer service, internet and related telecoms categories. The data provided does not name its specific products or customers, though firms of this type usually sell business broadband, voice and cloud communications. Reported funding is about 250 million, with the most recent entry in May 2021, which may be a debt facility or investment. A B2B telecom provider with low consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Markforged is a Waltham, Massachusetts maker of industrial 3D printers, best known for the Metal X system, which prints metal parts by bonding metal powder in plastic, and for carbon-fibre composite printers, with its Digital Forge software and cloud platform. Customers are manufacturers in aerospace, automotive, defence and tooling who print parts on demand, buying printers, materials and software subscriptions. Founded in 2013 by Greg Mark, it went public on the NYSE (MKFG) via a SPAC in 2021, with annual revenue of roughly 80 to 100 million dollars. Nano Dimension acquired it in 2025. B2B brand with little consumer awareness.

METiS Pharmaceuticals is a Hangzhou-based biotechnology company that presents itself as an AI-driven nanodelivery drug developer, using machine learning to design lipid and other nanoparticle systems that carry RNA and other medicines to specific tissues. Total funding of about 332 million dollars is reported through August 2025. It is private, and customers would be pharma partners and eventually patients through its own pipeline. Further detail on programmes, partners and staff cannot be confirmed from the data provided. A B2B biotech brand with little consumer awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

Milestone Pharmaceuticals is a Montreal-based cardiovascular drug developer, listed on Nasdaq (MIST) and the Toronto Stock Exchange. Its lead product, etripamil, is a fast-acting nasal spray that patients self-administer to stop episodes of paroxysmal supraventricular tachycardia (PSVT), a sudden fast heart rhythm, without going to hospital. The FDA approved it in late 2025 as Cardamyst after an earlier rejection, and the company is preparing the commercial launch in the US. Customers are cardiologists and emergency physicians, with patients as end users. Brand awareness is among heart specialists.

NextCure is a Beltsville, Maryland clinical-stage biotechnology company listed on Nasdaq (NXTC), originally a Johns Hopkins and Yale spin-out working on antibody immunotherapy discovery. It has since concentrated on LNCB74, an antibody-drug conjugate directed at the B7-H4 protein in cancers such as endometrial, breast and ovarian, after earlier programmes failed or were deprioritised. It has had past pharma collaborations, and reports no product revenue. Customers would be oncologists if drugs are approved. Brand awareness is confined to biotech investors and cancer researchers.

PepGen is a Boston clinical-stage biotechnology company listed on Nasdaq (PEPG), developing oligonucleotide therapies attached to cell-penetrating peptides, called Enhanced Delivery Oligonucleotides, to treat serious neuromuscular and neurological diseases. Its leading candidates are PGN-EDODM1 for myotonic dystrophy type 1 and PGN-EDO51 for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, with a patient base of rare disease communities. It reports no product revenue. Funding totals about 355 million dollars. Brand awareness is among rare disease clinicians and biotech investors, with none among consumers.

Rani Therapeutics is a San Jose, California clinical-stage biotherapeutics company that has developed the RaniPill, an ingestible capsule that delivers biologic drugs such as antibodies and peptides through the intestinal wall so they can be taken orally rather than by injection. Its candidates include RT-102 for osteoporosis, an oral GLP-1 type obesity programme and partnerships with Novartis, Chugai and others. Founded in 2012 by Mir Imran and listed on Nasdaq (RANI), it has no marketed product. Brand awareness is among drug delivery experts and biotech investors, not consumers.

Redcare Pharmacy, formerly Shop Apotheke Europe, is Europe's leading online pharmacy, with its legal base in the Netherlands (Sevenum, Limburg) and its main operations in Germany. It sells prescription and over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, beauty and health products through online shops in Germany, Austria, Switzerland, France, Italy, Belgium and the Netherlands, with annual sales above 2 billion euros and around 13 million active customers. Listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange and Xetra (RDC), it renamed itself in 2024 and has been rolling out its e-prescription services. Strong consumer brand in German-speaking markets, advertising widely.

Smile Telecoms Holdings is a Mauritius-registered operator of mobile broadband networks, known for Smile Communications, which launched 4G LTE data services in Africa in markets such as Uganda, Tanzania, Nigeria and the Democratic Republic of Congo, selling data bundles and devices to consumers and businesses. South African investor Remgro was a major shareholder, and the company sold or closed several of its operations from about 2019, with the group now more limited in scope. Based in Port Louis. The brand was known to broadband users in East and West Africa, and funding of about 365 million dollars dates from 2015.

Sonoma Biotherapeutics is a South San Francisco clinical-stage biotechnology company developing regulatory T cell (Treg) therapies to treat autoimmune and inflammatory diseases such as rheumatoid arthritis, hidradenitis suppurativa and vitiligo, and to protect transplants. It uses engineered Tregs that can be programmed to home to specific tissues, and it entered a major collaboration with Regeneron in 2024 and an earlier one with Gilead's Kite. Founded in 2019, it is privately held and venture-backed, with total funding of about 365 million dollars. Brand awareness is limited to biotech circles.

Surrozen is a South San Francisco biotechnology company, listed on Nasdaq (SRRK), developing antibody drugs that modulate the Wnt signalling pathway, which controls tissue repair, to regenerate damaged tissue in the liver, intestine and eye. Its lead candidates have included SZN-043 for alcoholic hepatitis and SZN-413 for retinal disease, and it has a partnership with Boehringer Ingelheim. It became public through a 2021 SPAC merger with Consonance-HFW. Funding of about 365 million dollars is reported. Its pipeline is in early to mid-stage trials, with no product revenue. Brand awareness is among biotech investors only.

TELA Bio is a Malvern, Pennsylvania medical technology company that sells soft-tissue reconstruction products, notably the OviTex and OviTex PRS reinforced tissue matrices that are used in hernia repair and breast reconstruction, made from sheep tissue layered with polymer. Customers are hospitals and surgeons, with annual sales of roughly 60 to 70 million dollars. Founded in 2012 and listed on Nasdaq (TELA), it employs a sales force across the US. Brand awareness is among general and plastic surgeons, not consumers.

Umoja Biopharma is a biopharmaceutical company, originating in Boulder, Colorado and based in Seattle, that develops in vivo cell therapy, in which a virus-like delivery system programs a patient's own immune cells inside the body to attack cancer without the need for separate cell manufacturing. Its platform includes UB-VV111 CD19-directed in vivo CAR-T, and it has an AbbVie partnership. Privately held, with total funding of about 363 million dollars, it has no product revenue. Brand awareness is among cell therapy specialists and biotech investors.

Virgin Hyperloop was a Los Angeles company developing a hyperloop passenger and cargo transport system, in which pods travel in low-pressure tubes at very high speed. It grew from Hyperloop One, and Richard Branson's Virgin Group became the lead investor in 2017, with DP World also a major backer. It ran a test track in Nevada and carried its first passengers in 2020, then dropped passenger plans to focus on cargo, cut most staff and shut down at the end of 2023. Funding was about 368 million dollars. The Virgin brand gave it high public visibility, though it never operated commercially.

Yellow Cake plc is a London-based Jersey-incorporated investment company listed on the AIM market of the London Stock Exchange (YCA), whose purpose is to hold physical uranium (U3O8) as a way for investors to gain exposure to the uranium price. It buys uranium from Kazatomprom under a supply agreement and stores it at conversion facilities, with net assets in the hundreds of millions of pounds and a small management team at Yellow Cake's adviser Tavira. Customers are shareholders, and it does not mine. B2B finance business with little consumer awareness.

6K is a North Andover, Massachusetts advanced materials company that uses a microwave plasma process called UniMelt to turn recycled and virgin feedstock into powders for batteries and additive manufacturing. Its 6K Energy business supplies cathode materials such as LFP and NMC for lithium-ion batteries, and 6K Additive supplies metal powders for 3D printing in aerospace, medical and industrial uses. Founded in 2007 as a spin-out, it has raised over 300 million dollars with backers including Stonepeak and US Department of Energy support. B2B materials brand with low consumer awareness.

AeroFarms is an American vertical farming company, founded in 2004 and best known for growing leafy greens indoors in stacked trays using aeroponic misting rather than soil or sunlight, sold under the Dream Greens brand in US grocery stores. It operated large indoor farms in New Jersey and Virginia and had a research partnership in Abu Dhabi, backed by investors including Ingka and Goldman Sachs. After heavy losses it filed for Chapter 11 in June 2023 and later emerged from bankruptcy with a leaner business, with funding of about 314 million dollars. Moderate US grocery brand visibility.

Aiage is a Chinese health and biotechnology company in Nanning, Guangxi, whose Crunchbase description says it develops longevity-related products based on intestinal flora and other anti-ageing science. Funding of CN yuan 2.25 billion, around 300 million dollars, is shown for May 2025.
